## First-cycle placement schedule

Assuming a single-cycle flock from 17 through 80 weeks, with no induced molt:

- **T−8 to T−6 weeks:** Have the equipment supplier and UEP auditor confirm the usable-area drawing, expressly excluding required nest area. Reissue the board placement authorization at no more than the verified usable square footage.
- **T−6 to T−4:** Confirm strain, aviary-reared source, chain-feeder and nipple familiarity, vaccination program, beak-treatment certificate, delivery date and contract tolerances.
- **T−4 to T−2:** Commission ventilation, alarms, generator, belts, feed delivery, water-meter and pressure regulation. Update the emergency, depopulation, biosecurity and flock-training SOPs for House 7.
- **T−14 days:** Receive pullet body-weight/uniformity report, vaccination record, health documentation and rear-house lighting/feed schedule. Pullets should preferably come from an aviary rearing system.
- **T−7 days:** Clean and disinfect; verify downtime; potable-water test; flush lines; calibrate feed and water meters; test every belt, nest and alarm circuit.
- **Day 0, age 17 weeks:** Place the complete flock in one delivery window if practical. Match the rear-house day length initially; immediately establish water access, then feed, and check bird distribution and crops.
- **Days 1–7:** Trigger nipples as needed, record feed/water twice daily, inspect all tiers, retrieve mortality, and make evening rounds to return floor birds to the system.
- **Weeks 18–24:** Transition from pre-lay to peak ration according to production and body weight. Open and manage nests before expected lay; collect floor eggs several times daily. Increase light gradually toward 16 hours—do not jump directly to 16L on arrival.
- **Approximately weeks 26–32:** Peak-production period. Operate 16L:8D if consistent with the strain program, with staged dawn/dusk. UEP permits 8–18 hours of continuous light and requires staged dimming before dark. [UEP lighting requirements](https://uepcertified.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/2024-UEP-Revised-CF-Guidelines-Final.pdf)
- **Weeks 32–80:** Phase-feed against egg mass, intake and shell quality; weekly production review; periodic body-weight, feather and keel monitoring.
- **Week 80:** End-of-lay catch and removal, followed by full litter removal, wash/disinfection, repairs and documented downtime.

UEP permits initial internal confinement for training for up to six weeks, but the duration should be the shortest that produces reliable system and nest use. All required placement dates and any confinement must be recorded.

### Resource and equipment checks

At 30,000 hens, the minimum UEP quantities are:

- Usable area: 30,000 ft², excluding required nest space from the new-equipment calculation.
- Nipples: 3,000 minimum. The specified 10 birds/nipple is compliant.
- Accessible straight-trough edge: 45,000 linear inches, or 3,750 ft, where hens access both sides. Four runs cannot be approved without their actual length and accessible sides.

- Litter/scratch area: at least 4,500 ft².
